transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Um… thanks. I guess I’m here because my eating has been feeling kind of out of hand lately. Mostly when I’m alone at night—once I start, it’s like something takes over, and I can’t really stop, even though I’m telling myself to just put the food away. I know that probably sounds… I don’t know, but it’s been worrying me.
How do you feel after one of these episodes of eating when you can't stop?

I feel… really awful, honestly. Embarrassed, mostly. And panicky, like I’ve messed everything up.

Um… I don’t really like saying this, but after it happens I usually go to the bathroom and make myself throw up. It feels, in the moment, like the only way to sort of… undo it before the calories settle in. I know that’s not good. I’m sorry, I’m trying to be honest.
How often do these episodes of eating when you can't stop happen?

Um… I guess it’s been more than just occasional. For the last four months or so, there’s usually been at least one night a week where I’m by myself and I eat way more than I meant to. And then… afterward I make myself throw up. I know that’s not great, but that’s the pattern, I think.
Do you worry about gaining weight?

Yeah… I mean, probably more than I should. I try to tell myself it’s just normal concern, but if the scale is even like a pound up after a shift, or my work pants feel a little tighter, it can kind of ruin my whole day.

I start thinking I’m letting myself get fat, and then I’m… planning how I’m going to make up for it. I know that probably sounds a bit much.
Is making yourself throw up mostly to prevent weight gain?

Yeah… I think so. I don’t like admitting that, but after I eat like that, I usually end up in the bathroom making myself throw up because it feels like the only way to undo it before the calories… settle in, I guess.

I know that probably sounds bad. I’m not trying to be dramatic — it just feels really urgent in the moment.
Do you think your weight or body shape is different from how others see it?

I… yeah, I think so. I mean, I know other people probably don’t look at me and see what I see, or they’d say I’m being too hard on myself.

But when I’m in the bathroom mirror at home, it’s like all I can focus on is my stomach and my waist. If they look… wrong, or bigger than I think they should, I feel like I’ve messed up somehow, like I wasn’t disciplined enough. Even if I had a good day at the rescue center and did everything right there, that part can still make me feel like I failed.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your weight over the past few months?

I’m not totally sure, honestly. I mean, I check, but it kind of goes up and down, and I don’t know if I’d call it “significant.” Maybe it feels significant to me when it changes a little, but I’m not sure it would look that way to someone else.

Is that… the kind of thing you mean?
Do you ever exercise excessively to try to burn off calories after one of these episodes?

I don’t think so… not in a big way. I mean, I might walk around more or feel restless afterward, but I wouldn’t say I’m doing intense workouts to make up for it.

At least, I don’t think that’s what I’m doing. Is that what you mean by excessively?
Is your fear of gaining weight the main reason you try to undo the calories after eating?

Yeah… I think that’s probably the biggest part of it, even if I don’t like admitting that.

Like, if I get on the scale and it’s even a pound higher after a shift, or if my work pants feel tighter, I kind of latch onto it. I’ll tell myself it’s probably nothing, but then I spend the whole day worrying I’m letting myself get fat, and I start thinking about how I’m going to make up for it.

I know that probably sounds a bit extreme. But yes, I think the fear of gaining weight is a lot of what’s behind it.
Have you ever had a period where you didn't have these episodes of eating when you can't stop and then making yourself throw up?

I guess… not really, at least not lately.

For the last few months — maybe four months or so — it’s been pretty consistent. Usually at least one night a week, when I’m by myself, I end up eating way more than I meant to, and then afterward I make myself throw up.

I don’t love saying that. I keep wanting to say it’s not that bad because it’s not every day, but… yeah, it has been happening regularly.
Do you usually feel a lack of control during these episodes of eating when you can't stop?

Yeah… I think so. I wish I could say it’s just poor planning or being hungry, but once I’m alone at night and I start eating, it kind of feels like something takes over.

I’ll be telling myself, “Just put it away, stop now,” and I still keep going. It’s embarrassing to admit, but yes, it feels like I’m not really in control in those moments. Is that… is that the kind of thing you mean?
Do you also restrict your food intake between these episodes of eating when you can't stop?

I’m not totally sure how to answer that.

I don’t think I’m, like… formally restricting, if that makes sense? I don’t have a strict plan or anything. Sometimes I do try to “be good” the next day or eat lighter, but I haven’t really paid close attention to whether it’s a pattern.

Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Do you often eat very little during the day before one of these episodes of eating when you can't stop happens?

I’m not sure, honestly. I haven’t really tracked it that closely.

I mean… some days I might be busy at work and not eat much, but I don’t know if that’s specifically before it happens or just normal being busy. I wouldn’t want to say yes if I’m not sure.

I can try to pay more attention to that, if that would help.
Have you had any periods of significant weight loss followed by weight gain over the past year?

I don’t think so… not in any big, obvious way.

My weight maybe goes up and down a little, but I haven’t noticed, like, a major drop and then gaining it all back or anything. I don’t weigh myself super consistently, so I might not be the best judge, but nothing that stood out to me as significant.
Have you ever had a time when you lost a lot of weight and then gained it back?

Not that I can really think of, no. I mean, my weight has probably shifted a bit here and there, but I don’t remember a time where I lost a lot and then put it all back on.

I hope that answers it—I’m not trying to be vague, I just don’t think there’s been anything that dramatic.
Do you often skip meals or go for long periods without eating on purpose?

I don’t think I do it on purpose, no. I mean, I might miss a meal if work gets hectic or I’m distracted, but I wouldn’t say I’m intentionally trying to go a long time without eating.

At least… not that I’ve really noticed. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Do you ever feel like you need to exercise a lot to burn off the calories after one of these eating episodes?

Not really, no. I mean, I’m not someone who goes and works out for hours after eating or anything like that.

Sometimes I might feel like I should move around more if I feel uncomfortable after eating, but I wouldn’t say I’m exercising a lot specifically to burn it off. I hope that makes sense.
Do you feel like you're afraid of losing control over your eating during these episodes?

Yeah… I think that’s probably the part that worries me the most, if I’m being honest.

It’s usually when I’m alone at night. I’ll start eating, and at first I tell myself it’s just a little bit, but then it feels like something kind of takes over. Like I’m telling myself, “Okay, put it away now,” and I just… don’t. I can’t seem to stop in that moment.

I know that probably sounds bad. But yes, I guess I am afraid of losing control when it starts.
Have you experienced any significant weight fluctuations over the past year, such as losing and then regaining a substantial amount of weight?

I don’t think so… not anything I’d call substantial. My weight probably goes up and down a bit, like a few pounds here or there, but I haven’t really tracked it closely.

I mean, my clothes fit a little differently sometimes, but I wouldn’t say I’ve had a big loss and then gained it all back or anything. At least not that I’m aware of. Is that helpful?
Do you often try to limit the amount of food you eat on a typical day?

I’m not totally sure how to answer that. I don’t think I’m, like, formally dieting every day or counting everything.

I guess some days I’ll tell myself I should “be good” or keep things lighter, but I don’t know if that counts as trying to limit food. It’s not something I have a strict plan for, if that makes sense.
